scenes.text: Flamingos are not born pink. They turn pink because of what they eat.
Their color comes from pigments called carotenoids.
These are found in the algae and tiny crustaceans flamingos filter out of the water.
Brine shrimp are one of the best sources of that rosy color.
To eat, a flamingo turns its head upside down.
Its curved beak works like a strainer, catching food and pushing out the water.
The bird breaks down the pigments, and they end up in its growing feathers.
That's why flamingo chicks hatch white or gray.
For their first meals, both parents make a special liquid in their throats called crop milk.
It is rich in fat and protein, and it is bright pink or red.
Mom and dad pour so much color into eggs and crop milk that they can fade.
By the end of a breeding season, some parents look almost white.
Scientists also think standing on one leg may help flamingos save body heat or energy.
There are six species of flamingo in the world.
And in Africa, some colonies have more than a million birds.
If you were colored by your favorite food, what color would you be?

title: Flamingos are pink because of what they eat 🦩
caption: Flamingo chicks hatch white or gray. The pink comes from carotenoid pigments in algae and brine shrimp. 🦐
